---
title: "Operations"
---

## Operations define the reusable unit

Cellerator grows through reusable mathematical operations and the structure,
layout, preparation, and execution semantics that make those operations useful
for cellular models. Group by operation contract, not by one application.
Each operation should state accepted identities and shapes, output and
derivative behavior, precision, backend, preparation and reuse rules, and
complete-cost evidence.

Product2 computes one output for each declared input pair:

\[ y_i = c_i x_{a_i} x_{b_i} \]

There is no reduction across pairs. The “2” names the operation arity (two indexed
state inputs), not a version. The Python `cellerator.ops` module currently
exposes native CPU Product2 and forward/JVP/VJP entry points. The optional Torch package exposes
the same operation through `product2` and `Product2Module`; its current
autograd implementation is first-order and CPU FP32. The native Product2
implementation still lives under the current `src/compute` and `src/execution`
routes. The target operation-family layout does not change that current source
ownership until a complete move is reviewed.

Other native and Torch-backed operation families exist in sparse support,
mechanism, matrix, process, tokenization, and related areas. Their existence
does not make them one package-wide API with shared maturity. Consult each
facility's own contract and evidence:

- [Sparse support foundation](sparse_support_foundation.qmd) covers explicit
  support/index/routing and synthetic ranked-gene/event operations.
- [Tokenization](tokenization.qmd) covers optional ATen tensor and sequence
  operations.
- [Python bindings](development/python-bindings.md) describes native Product2,
  optional Torch indexed-mechanism support, resident CUDA, sparse support, and
  tokenization boundaries.
- The [source routing map](development/routing.md) is the exhaustive current
  path and consumer inventory.

The opt-in prepared entity-to-mechanism route query now has a native host index,
CUDA query implementation, and Python/Torch adapter. It reuses reverse postings
and checks caller-supplied owner, relation, structure, route, and binding
generations. The existing route policy is consumed as supplied. CPU/native and
adapter checks pass, as do the 16-test suite, exact CUDA correctness check, and
memcheck, racecheck, and synccheck for the frozen binary. A source-bound V100
measurement found a 9.21% median horizon-64 lifecycle improvement over the
Python route for synthetic ranked `[32,8]` inputs; the event result was
inconclusive, and dense Torch won on the larger stress shapes. The prepared
path remains opt-in, with Python as the default. See the
[qualification report](https://github.com/tumlinso/Cellerator/blob/94c534fc794fe8cc3e0434e4a50f379401ddbb3c/bench/sparse_support/experiments/prepared_routing/REPORT.md)
for its scope and limits before considering a model-level default.

## How new families should fit

Keep the operation contract model-neutral and compose it with Torch where
Torch already supplies the surrounding machinery. Prefer a Cellerator module
when users need a stable model-level composition, owned parameters, or
operation-specific preparation. Keep the derivative implementation aligned
with the forward operation and test repeated identities, invalidation, and
layout conversions explicitly. Add an operation family as real source and
consumers arrive; do not add placeholder modules or promise general backend
support ahead of implementation.
